description:
Get your brand's SpiderGate CAPACITY — per-provider key pressure and subscription windows.
Answers "do I need more keys?" and, just as often, "no — more keys will not help."

🔴 TWO BLOCKS, TWO DIFFERENT SCOPES — read the labels before quoting a number:
- key_pressure has traffic_scope="pool_wide". It counts every request on a key regardless of which
  tenant caused it, because a shared key serves the whole pool. It is NOT "your usage".
  Only the shared pool's keys are counted: no brand's private key is in these numbers.
- subscription_windows and the flow cross-tab are brand-scoped.

The `verdict` is the point, and it can REFUSE:
  healthy · add_keys · not_quota · account_capped · over_provisioned · unmeasurable
- not_quota — errors are high but they are NOT rate limits. Buying keys will not fix it;
  suggested_keys is deliberately null. Do not recommend keys on a not_quota verdict.
- account_capped — the cap is on the ACCOUNT, so one more key is refused identically.
- limit_source tells you whether headroom is published / partial / estimated_from_429.
  An estimate is not a published ceiling; say which one you used.

subscription_windows: DECIDE PER ROW, by `state` — not by the block flag.
- state "measured": `window_percent` is a number from 0 to 100. 0 is a reading (the window is open
  and has made no requests yet), not an absence.
- state "unmeasurable": `window_percent` is null and `reason` says why — one of
  no_plan_assigned · no_packages_for_provider · counter_incomparable · plan_has_no_published_cap ·
  lease_only_not_counted.
- A lease-only key (SpiderGate lends the login to your own CLI and sends no request on it) is
  never measured: its `window_percent` and both counts are null whatever plan it is on. Where it
  holds a request limit its reason is lease_only_not_counted. Do not report it as 0% or unused.
- `gauge_available` is derived on every response: true when at least one row is measured. With it
  true, other rows can still be unmeasurable. When it is false, `gauge_blocked_reason` is one
  sentence for a person; do not branch on its wording.
- `weekly_percent` is null on every row (no weekly counter is collected), and a window row's own
  `verdict` is always null — verdicts live on key_pressure rows.
- `window_tokens_counted` / `window_requests_counted` are null on a key with no window width
  (`window_hours` null or 0), and on every lease-only key. On any other key with a width,
  0 means nothing counted in this window yet.
- `can_set_plan` is true only for no_plan_assigned. A package then gives a percentage only if it
  publishes a request limit; one that does not reads plan_has_no_published_cap.
A field that is present and null is not 0 and not missing: test for null, and never render a null
as an empty gauge.
name: gate_capacity
